damped Euclidean SAGA with importance sampling p_i ~ L_i^(1/2) (combination of two published ingredients)

MISO with lower-bound surrogates (Mairal 2015; the Finito update with alpha = 1): iterate at the minimizer of the surrogate, i.e. the SAG direction with step 1 / lam; here with the relaxation delta of the table (delta = 1: MISO; delta < 1: dual-free SDCA, Shalev-Shwartz 2015; 'sdca' = lam n / (R2 + lam n), its largest admissible value)

damped SAGA (theta < 1) preconditioned by the feature covariance (combination of two published ingredients); control for the one-shot polar-metric B-SAGA
gradient descent, step c / L_F
Nesterov's accelerated gradient for strongly convex objectives, constant momentum; L = L_F / c, mu = c_mu lam
limited-memory BFGS (scipy L-BFGS-B, strong-Wolfe line search), one pass per evaluation of (F, grad F); memory m
full-batch nuclear-scaled polar step (stochastic spectral descent, Carlson et al. 2015; dualized steepest descent, Bernstein-Newhouse; PolarGrad, Lau-Long-Su), step <G, O> c / L_op
nuclear-scaled polar step of the SAGA estimator: W - gamma ||omega||_* polar(omega)

joint placement with the damped estimator m + theta c (theta = 1/n: polar factor of the SAG direction)
direction polar(omega), length gamma <m, polar(omega)>_+ (pairing with the predictable part)
joint placement with the bounded-gain map s / sqrt(s^2 + eps^2), eps = eps_innov ||theta c||_F
joint placement with importance sampling p_i ~ L_i^a of the index (weighted innovation)

gamma (sharp(m) + D sharp(m)[c]): innovation propagated through the Frechet derivative

SAGA preconditioned by the frozen polar metric of its predictable part (refreshed every n iterations): linear in the estimator, equal to the nuclear-scaled polar step at the anchor; step c / R2P (certified per-sample smoothness in the metric); gains floored at metric_floor < 1
loopless SVRG preconditioned by the frozen polar metric of the exact gradient at the reference point

SAGA preconditioned by the feature covariance, C proportional to (c_l Sigma_hat + lam I)^-1 with floored gains: the statistically preconditioned SAGA of the note B1 of the main project (the Newton metric for least squares), with the loss-part memory; control for the polar metric (the covariance, d^2 n operations, is not charged)
damped SAGA (theta < 1) preconditioned by the feature covariance (combination of two published ingredients); control for the one-shot polar-metric B-SAGA
gradient descent, step c / L_F
Nesterov's accelerated gradient for strongly convex objectives, constant momentum; L = L_F / c, mu = c_mu lam
limited-memory BFGS (scipy L-BFGS-B, strong-Wolfe line search), one pass per evaluation of (F, grad F); memory m
full-batch nuclear-scaled polar step (stochastic spectral descent, Carlson et al. 2015; dualized steepest descent, Bernstein-Newhouse; PolarGrad, Lau-Long-Su), step <G, O> c / L_op
nuclear-scaled polar step of the SAGA estimator: W - gamma ||omega||_* polar(omega)
nuclear-scaled polar step of the loopless-SVRG estimator
joint placement with the damped estimator m + theta c (theta = 1/n: polar factor of the SAG direction)
direction polar(omega), length gamma <m, polar(omega)>_+ (pairing with the predictable part)
joint placement with the bounded-gain map s / sqrt(s^2 + eps^2), eps = eps_innov ||theta c||_F
joint placement with importance sampling p_i ~ L_i^a of the index (weighted innovation)
bounded-gain joint placement with importance sampling p_i ~ L_i^(1/2)
gamma sharp(m) + gamma_c c: nuclear-scaled polar step of the predictable part, innovation added linearly
gamma (sharp(m) + D sharp(m)[c]): innovation propagated through the Frechet derivative
gamma sharp(grad F(w)) + gamma_c (innovation + lam (W - w)): one factorization per reference point
nuclear-scaled polar step of the PAGE / loopless-SARAH recursive estimator
gamma_c omega + gamma <omega, O_m> O_m with O_m = polar(m): Euclidean SAGA step plus a step along the predictable polar direction whose length is an unbiased estimate of <grad F, O_m>

SAGA preconditioned by the frozen polar metric of its predictable part (refreshed every n iterations): linear in the estimator, equal to the nuclear-scaled polar step at the anchor; step c / R2P (certified per-sample smoothness in the metric); gains floored at metric_floor < 1
loopless SVRG preconditioned by the frozen polar metric of the exact gradient at the reference point

SAGA preconditioned by the polar metric of the full gradient at W_0, computed once and never refreshed: SAGA on a fixed linear reparametrization of the problem (facts F10, F11), one factorization for the whole run
damped SAGA (theta < 1) preconditioned by the polar metric of the full gradient at W_0
Euclidean loopless SVRG plus one nuclear-scaled polar step (c_a / L_op) sharp(grad F(w)) at each refresh of the reference point (the nonlinear map sees exact gradients only)
joint placement with the table moved by the dual-free-SDCA fraction delta = lam n / (R2 + lam n) towards the fresh gradient instead of replaced

loopless Katyusha whose y step is the nuclear-scaled polar step of the estimator (the general-norm template of Allen-Zhu's Katyusha2 in the spectral norm); gamma_y = c / R2_op with c = 1/9 (the constant of Katyusha2) or 1; same (L, mu) grid as L-Katyusha
minibatch SAGA
damped minibatch SAGA
minibatch SAGA estimator, nuclear-scaled polar step
minibatch split placement
minibatch SGD, cosine schedule
Keller Jordan's Muon: momentum 0.95, Nesterov, 5 Newton-Schulz steps, fixed-length step, cosine schedule
MARS-M (Liu-Yuan-Gu), exact variant: same-batch correction g = 0.025 (two gradients per step), clip 1, momentum 0.95, cosine schedule
MARS-M (Liu-Yuan-Gu), approximate variant: correction with the gradient of the previous batch (one gradient per step), g = 0.025, clip 1, momentum 0.95, cosine schedule
STORM / MVR2 buffer (g = 1) then Newton-Schulz, cosine schedule (Chang et al.; Qian et al. arXiv:2512.16598)

STORM buffer with a norm-scaled step (variant of OptMuon-I, Yuan arXiv:2606.08783, which scales by the Frobenius norm times an AdaGrad-norm coefficient; here nuclear norm and constant gamma): removes the fixed-length floor, keeps the noise floor of the buffer
